hero.title: Write down every thesis. Let your past self become your best coach.
hero.subtitle: A stock compounding at 15% annually has a daily profit probability of just 50.02% — almost indistinguishable from a coin flip. Trading is never about any single outcome — it's about having enough records to validate your decision process. Markets don't reward effort, they reward capability — and capability comes from traceable decisions and honest reviews. Write, review, then compare with a partner — that's where the gap begins.
hero.description: A calm trading journal for active investors. Record your thesis, risk, execution and review — so every decision leaves a trace.

snapshot.title: Learning Snapshot
snapshot.description: Reviewing isn't optional — a loss you didn't learn from is just a loss. Log every market thesis on one timeline, then compare side by side with a partner. History doesn't repeat, but it rhymes.

learning.title: The Investor's Path
learning.subtitle: Markets don't reward effort, they reward capability. At the highest level, investing is less about financial knowledge and more about psychology. Know yourself before you try to know the market.

basics.title: Investment Identity & Awareness
basics.description: Not knowing whether you're a value investor or a price speculator is the root cause of many losses. Correct thinking doesn't guarantee profits, but wrong thinking virtually guarantees long-term losses.

risk.title: Position Sizing & Survival
risk.description: Offense determines your ceiling, but defense determines how long you stay in the game. A 25% drawdown requires a 33% gain just to break even — beyond that point, recovery becomes exponentially harder. Survival is the only prerequisite for compounding every edge you have. A 25% stop-loss on stocks and 5% on leverage are non-negotiable lines.

review.title: The Review Methodology
review.description: Top-down: news → global → index → sectors → individual stocks → update plan. Reviewing is when System 2 activates — the deliberate, energy-hungry thinking mode that actually corrects biases.

community.title: You don't have to trade alone
community.subtitle: Trade Basic's real value isn't just recording — it's putting your judgment and your partner's into the same review rhythm. System 1 makes snap decisions, System 2 corrects through review — and the loop itself is the engine that builds capability.

share.title: Account-level sharing
share.description: Turn on diary sharing for a partner link and both sides can compare history and new entries. Stock holdings are never exposed — your cards stay face-down.

feedback.title: Same-day side-by-side
feedback.description: Put both diaries next to each other on the same date. See who caught the key move and who missed the risk. No more arguing with vague impressions — let the written record speak.

accountability.title: AI can join the table
accountability.description: Issue a scoped API key to a partner account so an external agent can create diaries without inheriting full web access. Machine judgment plus your intuition — each covers the other's blind spots.

turnaround.title: From losses to consistency: turn process into edge
turnaround.subtitle: Success isn't measured by any single outcome — it's whether your decisions produce stable profits across enough repetitions. Let go of individual results and focus on decision quality.

step1.title: 1. Record your thesis
step1.description: Write down your rationale, risk assumptions, and trade plan while the market is still live. Don't wait until after the close — memory will rewrite the script for you.

step2.title: 2. Identify biases
step2.description: Compare execution results against your original hypothesis. Remember: making money once doesn't mean you've matured — a lucky profit can create the illusion of skill. Determine whether the decision was flawed or whether it was just variance. A correct process can still produce temporary losses.

step3.title: 3. Define rules
step3.description: Turn corrections into concrete, executable discipline rules. Sunk cost is never a reason to hold — learning to fold is the hardest and most important skill in investing.

step4.title: 4. Validate long-term
step4.description: Review rule effectiveness continuously. The ability to maintain discipline after consecutive losses is what separates novices from mature traders. Verify positive expectancy with at least 30 samples — one trade is random, a large sample is meaningful. The best starting hand in poker wins over 80% of the time — but still loses nearly 20%. Always leave room for error.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: Every feature serves one purpose: making your decision process reviewable, comparable, and optimizable

diary.title: Trading Diary
diary.description: Write every trade rationale, risk assumption, and market observation in Markdown. This is where System 2 kicks in — shifting from gut-reaction watching to deliberate, structured thinking.

stocks.title: Portfolio Management
stocks.description: Track holdings and average costs. Stock prices are deeply uncertain and every trader makes mistakes — position sizing is your last line of defense for error tolerance.

alerts.title: Smart Alerts
alerts.description: Set time-triggered reminders that force you to revisit key moments. Don't let important observations drown in the stream of time.

timeline.title: Timeline View
timeline.description: String every thesis into a traceable timeline. Review your own long-term rhythm first, then switch to same-day partner comparison when you need a sharper read.

partnerCompare.title: Partner Compare
partnerCompare.description: Human or AI — anyone can be a partner. Compare diaries side by side on the same day. Your blind spots are exactly what others can see. Holdings stay private.

security.title: Secure & Reliable
security.description: JWT + bcrypt + HttpOnly Cookie. Your trading data, like your edge, shouldn't be easy for anyone else to access.

themes.title: Dark Mode
themes.description: Support for dark and light themes. Long review sessions only work if they don't burn your eyes out.

cta.title: Your toughest opponent is never the chart — it's yourself
cta.description: Start logging today, review weekly, and bring in a partner when you're ready to stress-test your market read. When you're tilting, the prefrontal cortex shuts down and the amygdala takes over — System 1 makes snap judgments while System 2 gets dragged along. The only antidote is a plan written in advance and enough records to force System 2 online when you need it.

step1.label: Step 01
step1.title: Record
step1.description: Capture your rationale, risk assumptions, and stop-loss plan before every trade. Setting your stop before entry is non-negotiable.

step2.label: Step 02
step2.title: Review
step2.description: Compare outcomes with your original thesis. Separate decision flaws from random variance — not every loss means you were wrong.

step3.label: Step 03
step3.title: Refine
step3.description: Convert feedback into executable rules and verify positive expectancy with enough samples. Get the process right, and the results will follow.

cta.disclaimer: This platform is for education and review only, not investment advice. A reasonable annualized return of 6–10% is already hard-won. All investing carries risk, and outcomes vary by strategy and execution.

hero.title: About Me
hero.subtitle: Builder notes from a trader learning to walk with past experience

intro.title: Who I Am
intro.content: I am the developer of this site and a trader still learning every day. This project started as my own journal and evolved into a structured workflow for recording, reviewing, and improving decisions. Markets don't reward effort, they reward capability — and capability starts with acknowledging hindsight bias, then using written records to fight memory's tendency for self-editing.

motivation.title: Why I Built This
motivation.paragraph1: I used to repeat the same mistakes in emotional, low-discipline trades. Over time, I learned the real issue was not a lack of information, but the lack of a consistent process I could review. A loss you didn't learn from is just a loss — I didn't want any of my losses to go to waste.
motivation.paragraph2: This site is not built to promise quick wins. It is a practical training environment: log each decision, review it regularly, and refine your rules to reduce repeated errors while moving toward long-term goals like financial freedom and passive income.

pyramid.name: Pyramid (4-3-2-1)
pyramid.description: The most robust strategy, emphasizing a solid foundation. 40% base position at fair valuation or trend confirmation, then scale in.
cons: If base position is poorly timed, adding too fast during decline may lead to being trapped

pyramidVariant.name: Pyramid Variant (2-2-3-2-1)
pyramidVariant.description: Split the base position to reduce initial entry risk, suitable for volatile markets.
cons: Need more time to observe market

rectangular.name: Rectangular (3-3-3-1)
rectangular.description: Buy 30% three times, keep 10% cash as 'emergency fund' for black swan events.

invertedPyramid.name: Inverted Pyramid (1-2-3-4)
invertedPyramid.description: Minimal initial investment, then significantly increase. Suitable when highly confident in the target and expecting significant upside.
cons: Larger loss if judgment is wrong
